name: Trotskyism
info: Trotskyism is the branch of Marxism and Leninism developed by Leon Trotsky, built on permanent revolution, workers' democracy and internationalism; it took shape in Russia from 1905 and lives on in small parties and internationals worldwide.

facts.thinkers: Leon Trotsky, its founder and the head of the Fourth International; Isaac Deutscher, his biographer; Ernest Mandel, who argued that his economics differed from Stalin's forced collectivisation; James P. Cannon and Max Shachtman, the leading early American Trotskyists; Michel Pablo, whose theses split the Fourth International in 1953; Tony Cliff, Ted Grant and Gerry Healy in Britain
facts.texts: Trotsky's Our Political Tasks (1904), Results and Prospects (1906), Literature and Revolution, Problems of Everyday Life, The New Course (1924), The Stalin School of Falsification, The Revolution Betrayed (1936), Their Morals and Ours (1938), the Transitional Programme (1938) and In Defence of Marxism
facts.ideas: permanent revolution; the united front against fascism; workers' control and council democracy; a planned economy joined to workers' democracy; the transitional programme; proletarian internationalism; the analysis of the Soviet Union as a degenerated workers' state; uneven and combined development
facts.today: Small Trotskyist parties and internationals exist in many countries, among them the United Secretariat of the Fourth International, the International Committee of the Fourth International, the Committee for a Workers' International and the International Marxist Tendency; examples include Lutte Ouvrière in France, the Socialist Workers Party and Socialist Party in Britain, and the Left Bloc in Portugal

t: Trotsky formulated the theory of permanent revolution in 1905: in a backward country only the working class could overthrow feudalism, and it would then have to appeal to the workers of the advanced capitalist countries.
Trotskyists oppose Stalin's theory of socialism in one country and describe the Soviet Union after 1924 as a degenerated workers' state, ruled by a bureaucracy that suppressed democracy.

Trotsky was expelled from the Soviet Union in 1929 and founded the Fourth International in 1938; he was attacked in Mexico City on 20 August 1940 by Ramón Mercader, an NKVD agent, and died the next day.
dyk: The word Trotskyism was coined, according to Trotsky, by the Russian liberal leader Pavel Milyukov, who fought it "as early as 1905"; in 1917 Lenin's April Theses were themselves condemned by his opponents as Trotskyist.
ev: Trotsky chairs the St. Petersburg Soviet and formulates the theory of permanent revolution
Trotsky joins the Bolsheviks in July and leads the Military Revolutionary Committee that carries out the October insurrection
Trotsky is removed from power in October and expelled from the Communist Party in November
Trotsky is expelled from the Soviet Union after exile to Alma-Ata in 1928
The Fourth International is founded in Paris and adopts Trotsky's Transitional Programme
Ramón Mercader attacks Trotsky in Mexico City on 20 August; Trotsky dies the next day
The Fourth International splits into two public factions over the theses of Michel Pablo
The International Secretariat and some sections of the International Committee reunify

sections.origins:
Trotskyism arose from the Russian revolutionary movement of the early 20th century. According to Trotsky, the term was coined by Pavel Milyukov, the leader of the Constitutional Democratic Party, who attacked it "as early as 1905". In that year Trotsky was elected chairman of the St. Petersburg Soviet during the Russian Revolution of 1905 and pursued a policy of proletarian revolution, at a time when other socialist currents advocated a transition to a bourgeois regime to replace the essentially feudal Romanov state. He formulated the theory of permanent revolution in 1905 and set it out at length in Results and Prospects (1906).

Trotsky's early relations with Lenin were mixed. They were close personally before the London Congress of 1903 and again during the First World War, and Trotsky initially opposed some aspects of Leninism. His book Our Political Tasks (1904) warned of the dangers of substitutionism in a Leninist party model. Before February 1917 he had not accepted the importance of a Bolshevik-style organisation; once the revolution broke out he did, and he joined the Bolsheviks in July 1917.

The phrase "legend of Trotskyism" is Trotsky's own, for what he said Grigory Zinoviev and Lev Kamenev formulated with Stalin in 1924 against his criticisms of Politburo policy.
sections.ideas:
Trotsky said that five elements distinguished his programme from other Marxist theories: permanent revolution, opposed to the two-stage theory of his opponents; criticism of the post-1924 leadership of the Soviet Union and, after 1933, support for a political revolution there; social revolution in the advanced capitalist countries through working-class mass action; proletarian internationalism; and a transitional programme of demands bridging daily struggles and the socialist transformation of society.

Permanent revolution held that the capitalist class of a backward country, tied to feudal landowners and to foreign capital, was incapable of carrying through a bourgeois revolution. The working class would do so, win the support of the peasantry, set up a workers' state and appeal to workers abroad; the revolution had to spread, since a socialist state in Russia could not hold out alone. Trotsky also took the word from Marx's address of March 1850. The theory was joined by the concept of uneven and combined development.

Trotsky favoured a vanguard party, council democracy, workers' control of production, a planned economy with decentralisation, voluntary collectivisation, a united front against fascism and cultural autonomy for the arts. Trotskyists call states with state-owned economies but no democracy degenerated or deformed workers' states.
sections.spread:
After Lenin's strokes of 1922 to 1924, Trotsky criticised the Politburo and the bureaucratisation of the party; in 1923 he and a number of Old Bolsheviks signed the Declaration of 46. Zinoviev and Kamenev joined him in the United Opposition in 1926. Trotsky was removed from power in October 1927, expelled from the party in November, exiled to Alma-Ata in January 1928 and expelled from the Soviet Union in February 1929; he then moved from Turkey to France, Norway and Mexico. He founded the International Left Opposition in 1930, renamed the International Communist League in 1933, and the Fourth International followed in Paris in 1938.

At that founding Trotskyism was a mass current in Vietnam and Sri Lanka and, slightly later, Bolivia, and a substantial movement in China included Chen Duxiu. Its Vietnamese leader Tạ Thu Thâu was captured and executed by the Viet Minh in September 1945. After 1945 the movement was smashed in Vietnam and marginalised elsewhere. The Fourth International split in 1953 over Michel Pablo's theses, and the two factions were reunified in 1963 as far as the International Secretariat and some sections of the International Committee were concerned. Other internationals followed, among them the Committee for a Workers' International, founded in 1974.
sections.power:
Trotskyist parties did not come to govern a state, so the record in power is that of Trotsky himself in the Russian Revolution and Civil War. He led the Military Revolutionary Committee in October 1917 and was the Red Army's paramount leader afterwards. Critics point to his record in the period of war communism, including the militarisation of labour, concentration camps for war prisoners and the Red Terror. Trotsky defended his military decisions as necessary, comparing them to Abraham Lincoln's ruthlessness; Isaac Deutscher noted that he preferred to exchange hostages and prisoners rather than execute them.

The suppression of the Kronstadt rebellion, which Trotsky as leader of the Red Army and the other Bolsheviks repressed brutally, remained a point of attack. Trotsky argued that the sailors' attitudes and social composition had changed during the Civil War. He accepted the ban on rival parties in Moscow during the Civil War but opposed extending it to the Mensheviks in Soviet Georgia.

Trotskyists were themselves victims of Stalinist rule. Almost all Trotskyists within the party were executed in the Great Purges of 1937 to 1938, and in the Spanish Civil War Stalinist-directed NKVD purges struck the Trotskyist-aligned POUM, among them the execution of Andreu Nin. Trotsky was assassinated in 1940.
sections.critiques:
Trotskyism has been attacked from several directions. Marxist–Leninists such as Moissaye J. Olgin in 1935 called it "the enemy of the working class", and Harry Haywood argued that Trotsky lost because his ideas failed to conform to objective conditions. Fidel Castro said in 1966 that Trotskyism had become "a vulgar instrument of imperialism and reaction". Left communists such as Paul Mattick held that the October Revolution was totalitarian from the start, so that Trotskyism differs little from Stalinism; the Trotskyist historian Pierre Broué rejected this. Anarchists such as Emma Goldman and Dwight Macdonald, who left the American Socialist Workers Party, raised Trotsky's part in the Kronstadt repression.

Historians dispute whether Trotsky was a forerunner of Stalinism. Robert Service, Dmitri Volkogonov and others contend that he shared the same totalitarian strand of thought; George Orwell doubted that there was much difference. Jeffrey Meyers replied that Trotsky opposed Stalin's dictatorship from 1924 to 1940. Sheila Fitzpatrick found it implausible that Trotsky would have launched the Great Purges, while Richard B. Day, Vadim Rogovin and Robert Vincent Daniels saw him as a more democratic alternative. Baruch Knei-Paz and Victor Serge noted some affinities in the use of coercion together with clear differences.
sections.legacy:
Trotskyists drew on Lenin's testament and his alliance with Trotsky in 1922 to 1923 as evidence that Lenin wished to remove Stalin as General Secretary. Scholars such as E. H. Carr, Isaac Deutscher, Moshe Lewin and Ronald Suny held that Lenin's desired heir would have been a collective responsibility in which Trotsky had an important role. Sheila Fitzpatrick reported a scholarly consensus that Stalin appropriated the Left Opposition's positions on industrialisation and collectivisation, while Ernest Mandel argued that Trotsky's plan differed from Stalin's collectivisation in its brutality.

Trotsky's writings influenced others: Literature and Revolution has been called by Robert Bird the first systematic treatment of art by a Communist leader, his Manifesto for an Independent Revolutionary Art of 1938 was endorsed by André Breton and Diego Rivera, and Stafford Beer was reported to have read his critique of the Soviet bureaucracy while working on Project Cybersyn.

Trotskyist parties remain small. Examples include the Revolutionary Communist Party in Britain from 1944, the Socialist Workers Party founded by Tony Cliff, Militant's effective control of Liverpool City Council in the 1980s, Argentina's Workers' Left Front, and the Left Bloc in Portugal, which won 10.19% of the vote in 2015. In France in 2002 three Trotskyist candidates ran in the presidential election, Arlette Laguiller of Lutte Ouvrière winning 5.72%.

summary: Trotskyism is the Marxist current developed by Leon Trotsky, centred on permanent revolution, workers' democracy and internationalism, and opposed to Stalin's socialism in one country. Trotsky was exiled in 1929 and murdered in 1940, and its parties and internationals have since remained small.
references: Robert J. Alexander, International Trotskyism, 1929–1985: A Documented Analysis of the Movement (Duke University Press, 1991)
Isaac Deutscher, The Prophet: The Life of Leon Trotsky (Verso Books, 2015)
Baruch Knei-Paz, The social and political thought of Leon Trotsky (Clarendon Press, 1978)
Joshua Rubenstein, Leon Trotsky: a revolutionary's life (Yale University Press, 2011)
